body:
I think that it is not a defect.
CakePHP doesn't know what is correct. It is depend on application.
For instance http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki// is not the same as http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/
You can get rid of the double slash using url rewriting.

I can think of a couple of userland workarounds, that's not the issue. I think the framework should protect the user from this.

Considering cakephp.org is the offical website and is suffering from this "defect" shows it's an issue easily overlooked, so why not let the framework protect the developer from this error? My bet is nobody actually wants their apps to respond to /this-url and //this-url at the same time - and certainly not for the same ressource.

I would prefer http://cakephp.org//services to respond with a 404, unless there is a Router::connect('//services', ...) in the routes.php.

I am with @biesbjerg if there is an easy enough solution to it.
I mentioned this quite a while back in http://www.dereuromark.de/2012/12/29/cakephp-and-seo/#appendix
But most (and even I dont use that for 90% of the apps) are not aware of the issue at all.
So while I can update the default `.htaccess` rules provided with the framework, we'd also need to update the docs for nginx and iis.

@dereuromark I tried using the `.htaccess` rules on your blog but they never ended up matching the request URIs. Before the URLs reached mod_rewrite the // had already been stripped out.

```
$ curl -I 'cake.localhost//tasks/add'
```

I had setup CakePHP inside a virtual host with the document root set to `app/webroot`. I tried with Apache 2.2.26.
With no updates I can't look into this any further. Closing until there is a way to reproduce or a patch to fix it.

@markstory I think that this issue is related to [lines 136-138 of CakeRequest](https://github.com/cakephp/cakephp/blob/67ba9cb40623deeddf6326c9ccff09afc27be447/lib/Cake/Network/CakeRequest.php#L136-L138).
In fact we cannot access http://cakephp.org///services.

Yes, I can access the page with `//` but not with `///` as well. The line you cited was added in aa234bc8610430211cfd621822e144ba285bc2e3 to retain backwards compatibility. Removing that causes a number of tests around `$request->url` to fail as the value changes.
